summary: Short-lived session daisy-chain causes oscillatory GPU shortfall and p99 throughput regression
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on a small group of dedicated pools (NovaQ Analytics tenant) observed repeated p99 throughput regressions between 11:20-12:05 UTC on 2026-03-12. The pattern is a rapid series of short-lived inference sessions (median duration ~700ms) that chain through an internal multiplexer layer, causing a daisy-chain of allocator attach requests and transient slot hold times.

Impact:
- Intermittent p99 latency spikes and 10-30% throughput drop for the tenant's batched routes.
- Autoscales did not react quickly enough; allocator reported temporary slot exhaustion and denied new attaches.
- Some requests returned 5xx attach-timeout errors and a small percentage of early 429s from the tenant-level backpressure mechanism.

Environment:
- deployment: prod (us-west)
- pool: dedicated-usw2-03 (GPU type: A10x2 mixed inventory)
- model: redwood-open-7b-v1 pinned by customer

Steps to reproduce (observed in production):
1) The tenant issues high-rate short sessions from many small clients (fanout ~120 concurrent short streams).
2) Each session opens a connection and triggers allocator attach to a GPU slot; attach lifecycle includes sidecar-handshake + kv-prefetch + kv-cache-lock checks.
3) Rapid churn results in many attach operations queued in allocator, while sidecar log-flush tasks cause increased NVMe IO latency.
4) Autoscaler uses a 60s smoothing window and did not trigger fast enough; allocator hit transient slot depletion and started rejecting attaches.

Observed logs & metrics snippets:
- allocator.attach_time.p95 spike from 80ms -> 1.2s at peak
- gpu_slot_utilization dropped due to held-but-not-serving slots (ambiguous: 30% slots in 'attach' state)
- nvme_iowait increased by 3-4x on host snapshots coincident with sidecar flushes
- autoscaler.scale_decision lagged by ~45s due to metric smoothing

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Customer-side rate-limit applied to reduce small-session fanout to <60 concurrent short sessions (immediate improvement).
- Support lowered internal tenant priority to allow background housekeeping to proceed and freed several stuck attaches.

Notes: this ticket focuses on dedicated capacity behavior with noisy short-session fanout + sidecar IO coupling that produces oscillatory GPU shortfall. Full RCA pending.

investigation_notes:
Hypotheses:
- Primary: Short-session daisy-chain creates high attach-per-second rate; allocator serializes work for slot consistency resulting in spikes of 'attach' state that appear as held slots.
- Secondary: Sidecar log flush/housekeeping spike increases host IO latency, extending attach time and amplifying slot hold duration.
- Tertiary: Autoscaler smoothing prevents fast scale-up. Together these produce oscillatory shortfalls.

Evidence collected:
- Allocator traces show surge of attach RPCs queued; median queue length increased from 3 -> 48 during incidents.
- Host iostat/NVMe samples align with sidecar flush cron at :20 and :50 each minute.
- Autoscaler decisions deferred due to 60s window; when smoothing reduced, scale-up happens within 10-15s.

Immediate actions in flight:
- PR #4482 (runtime): add optimistic attach path allowing concurrent metadata read for short sessions (in code review).
- PR #119 (autoscaler): introduce short-session detection profile with lower smoothing for pools tagged 'burst-short-sessions'.
- Sidecar tweak: change log-flush stagger and backoff to avoid synchronized host-level flush at fixed minute marks.

Monitoring & validation plan:
- Add allocator.attach_queue_length alert (>20 sustained for 30s).
- Temporarily monitor NVMe iowait per-host and correlate with attach_time.
resolution:
In progress - temporary mitigations reduced customer impact: tenant admission cap and customer-side throttling. Implemented autoscaler smoothing override for pool (reduced to 10s) which cut scale-up latency from ~60s to ~12s; this reduced p99 spikes. Runtime PR to improve attach concurrency merged to staging and scheduled for canary on weeknight.

Follow-ups (action items):
- Merge and roll out runtime optimistic attach path across dedicated pools (ENG-2543).
- Add pool tag and autoscaler profile to detect short-session fanouts automatically (ENG-2561).
- Update dedicated runbook: add guidance for admission caps and temporary smoothing overrides.
- Coordinate with customer to adopt client-side connection pooling to reduce fanout.

Will update ticket when canary looks healthy in production and final postmortem is published on confluence.
